answer.rationale: The p99 write-path latensy spike is confined to the primary region and a release went out 2 hours ago. memory_b1 shows a prior release rollback cleared a checkout error spike without customer impact. memory_b2 shows regional failover restored latency fast but is more disruptive. A rollback is the least-invasive intervention that directly addresses the most likely cause (the recent release) while preserving all customer writes. Regional failover would also work but carries higher risk to in-flight settlement writes at daily peak. Circuit breakers and read-replica routing do not address a write-path degradation. Adding capacity does not address a regression. Therefore, rollback_release maximizes sustained availability without losing customer writes.
